transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-07-30
Start: 14:00 PDT
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Lena, Samir, Maya (Redwood) / Rajiv, Nikki, Darren, Sophie, Tommy (Kayden)

Auto Summary (auto-gen, may be rough): go over MSA DPA expectations, SLA tiers, and pricing pathway. customer wants clarity on KMS, SSO, and if private deploy needed for PII flows.

[00:00] Lena Ortiz (Redwood AE): thanks everybody for joining. I'm Lena from Redwood. quick round robin?
[00:05] Rajiv Kapoor (Kayden): Rajiv, head of procurement. morning.
[00:08] Nikki Torres (Kayden Legal): Nikki, legal counsel.
[00:10] Darren Li (Kayden Platform): Darren, platform eng.
[00:12] Sophie Grant (Kayden Security): Sophie, security.
[00:14] Tommy Reed (Kayden Finance): Tommy, finance — here for pricing approvals.
[00:16] Samir Patel (Redwood SE): Samir, solutions eng — I'll cover technical bits.
[00:18] Maya Chen (Redwood CSM): Maya, CSM, hi.

[00:30] Lena: ok, quick agenda: MSA/DPA redlines, SLA options, keying/SSO, pricing approval path, and pilot. want to make sure we line up the stakeholders so procurement knows who signs.
[00:40] Rajiv: yep that's the meat. our procurement team will not sign to a vendor without legal and finance signoff. timeline wise, we want a pilot in august and procurement signoff by sept end. can that work?
[00:48] Lena: that's tight but reasonable. pilot in august — we can do a short 2-week pilot with a scoped workload. Samir will outline infra choices; we can do hosted with VPC peering or a dedicated pool.

[01:10] Samir: quick technical, we typically offer hosted (fast on-ramp) and Dedicated (reserved GPU capacity) — Dedicated gives more predictable latency and data isolation. for PII flows, we usually recommend Private / VPC or customer-managed keying.
[01:30] Darren: can you clarify "customer-managed keying" — do you mean HSM or KMS? we have GCP KMS and use CMEK for storage.
[01:35] Samir: yes CMEK support — we can integrate with customer's KMS via our private control plane in the Dedicated offering; for on-prem, we also have an on-prem package but that's heavier. apologies, sometimes the exported notes say 'KV cache' but I mean 'KV cache' as runtime cache not keying.
[01:55] Sophie: we need details around key access, rotation, audit logs. also encryption-in-transit + at-rest is table stakes. what about SOC2 / ISO?
[02:05] Lena: Redwood maintains SOC2 Type II and we're in process for ISO 27001 — we'll send the certs. our security pack includes penetration test summary, SOC attestation, and a data flow diagram.
[02:20] Nikki: on the DPA — we have a couple redlines: 1) data deletion timelines for ephemeral logs, 2) subprocessor list and notification period, 3) carve-outs around law enforcement requests — anything unusual?
[02:35] Lena: that's fair — our standard DPA has 30-day deletion for customer logs, subprocessors are listed in the security pack and we notify within 30 days for changes. law enforcement requests: we require a legal process and will notify unless prohibited. if you need shorter deletion windows we can discuss, but that can affect how we do prefix caching and observability.
[02:55] Nikki: procurement will push on deletion SLA and egress fees. can you confirm egress pricing model?
[03:05] Tommy: yes finance needs that clearly. we have an internal rate card we use.
[03:10] Lena: high level egress is per-GB transfer for model payloads beyond baseline; tokens are billed per token for hosted. for pilot we typically offer a reduced trial credit; we'll include example cost scenarios in the spreadsheet Samir mentioned.

[03:45] Samir: technical tradeoffs: Dedicated lowers variance in latency — if you need 99th percentile low latency, Dedicated + local quantization or a slightly smaller model variant helps. Hosted with caching can also meet many SLAs depending on traffic pattern.
[04:05] Darren: our traffic pattern is lots of short queries, some long generation for customer support summarization. latency spike tolerance is low, we need p99 under 400ms for short queries ideally.
[04:18] Samir: 400ms p99 is achievable on Dedicated depending on model and sequence length; we'll put numbers in the perf sheet. caveat: on cold starts and large batches p99 can vary.
[04:35] Sophie: audit logs — we need per-request logs for 90 days and ability to redact PII, and SAML SSO for admin.
[04:45] Lena: SAML/SSO is supported, RBAC for team roles, and log retention can be configured — default is 30 days but enterprise packages extend to 90/365. redaction is a mix of runtime heuristics and customer-side filters; we can outline the redaction options.

[05:20] Nikki: on MSA commercial terms — liability caps, IP carveouts, and support SLA windows. our legal team will propose a redline. is Redwood open to limited liability carveouts for regulated data?
[05:35] Lena: we have standard liability language but can discuss carveouts for highly regulated data under a Private deployment and additional indemnities; Redwood legal handles on a case-by-case basis. we'll bring legal into the redline session.

[06:00] Tommy: pricing approval — our procurement needs a single summary sheet with net of discounts, pilot credits, and estimated run rate. can you provide a conservative and an optimistic estimate?
[06:12] Maya: yes we can provide both; Samir will help with conservative latency/cost numbers and Lena will provide the commercial side.

[06:40] Rajiv: who is the approver list? I need to get the approvers in the room for the legal redline workshop so it doesn't bounce later.
[06:48] Nikki: I'll pull them together — legal, procurement, finance.

[07:05] Lena: ok let's talk pilot scope — propose: 2 weeks, 100k requests total, sample dataset (anonymized), focus on short queries + summary flows; objective: demonstrate p95/p99 latency and confirm no data leakage.
[07:25] Darren: that seems reasonable. do you require us to move data to your hosted env? we prefer to keep PII out and send anonymized tokens; for the heavy flows we may want Dedicated with VPC peering.
[07:36] Samir: both are fine; pilot can be hosted with anonymized data and we can simulate production traffic. if you want Dedicated we can set up a small reserved pool but that takes longer to provision.

[08:10] Sophie: also want to confirm incident SLA and support windows — our ops is 24/7 so we need an escalation path.
[08:18] Lena: support tiers available; enterprise SLA includes 24/7 on-call with defined response times — we'll include that in the SLA options.

[08:40] Nikki: procurement will push on termination assistance and data escrow for continuity — are you offering data escrow or export tooling?
[08:50] Lena: export tooling yes, data export on request — escrow is available as an add-on / enterprise term. we'll document the migration / export process.

[09:12] Tommy: if we run a pilot and costs blow past estimates who covers excess? do you cap pilot spend?
[09:20] Lena: we set pilot budgets and usually provide a capped credit for the pilot; any overage is discussed and needs approval. we'll be explicit in the pilot statement of work.

[09:48] Samir: one more technical note — caching and KV prefix caching can reduce token cost and latency; it does mean certain prefixes get cached which impacts data residency slightly — meaning cached token info might live in runtime nodes for a short TTL.
[10:10] Sophie: TTLs? what are default retention windows for caches?
[10:15] Samir: defaults are short (seconds to minutes) but configurable; if you need zero runtime cache persistence we can configure that in Dedicated but it increases per-token compute.

[10:40] Lena: ok pulling back to procurement path: Rajiv, what are the formal gates? is it procurement review -> legal -> exec signoff?
[10:50] Rajiv: yes procurement reviews cost and third-party risk, then legal signs DPA/MSA and finance signs the PO. executive signoff might be needed for >$250k ARR.
[11:02] Lena: good to know. for the pricing approver list Nikki will share names and we will route the commercial term sheet accordingly.

[11:28] Nikki: on subprocessor transparency — we need a standing list and regular notification window at least 30 days before changes.
[11:36] Lena: we do 30-day notification and a posted subprocessor list in our trust portal; we'll send the link.

[12:00] Maya: logistics for next week: propose legal redline worksh op 60 minutes, include Kayden legal + procurement + Redwood legal. target Tue 2025-08-05 at 10am PT — does that work?
[12:10] Nikki: tentative yes, I'll confirm.

[12:30] Lena: action recap — we'll send security pack + sample MSA by Aug 1, Samir will send perf/cost sheet by Aug 4, Maya will schedule the redline workshop. any blockers?
[12:40] Darren: none on our side.
[12:42] Sophie: just want the SSO and retention docs up front.
[12:44] Lena: will include.

[13:05] Tommy: one last finance note — can Redwood provide a simple bill-of-materials for expected monthly run rate at 3 usage levels? low/med/high — that'll speed approvals.
[13:12] Samir: yes we'll include 3-run-rate scenarios.

[13:40] Rajiv: timeline summary: pilot in August, internal approval in Sept, aim for production in Q4 but flexible.
[13:48] Lena: got it.

[14:05] Maya: ok final Qs?
[14:08] Nikki: only that Redwood confirm indemnity language for regulated datasets — we'll flag exact text in the redline.
[14:12] Lena: we'll have legal present at redline.

[14:30] Lena: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the docs and Doodle for the workshop.
[14:33] (call ends)

Notes about transcription: speaker overlaps and some product names may be transcribed incorrectly (e.g., 'Dedicated' spelled differently, 'KV cache' transcribed as 'K V cache'). This transcript is an exported Fireflies style output and intentionally retains some imperfections.
